prompt: PC1 10.10.10.10/24 and PC2 10.10.10.20/24 are on active SW1 access ports in VLAN 10. ARP/ICMP are allowed; neither PC has a gateway. SW1 also connects R1--R2, with no routing protocol. Predict PC1 ping to PC2.
PC1 10.10.10.10/24 and PC2 10.10.10.20/24 share active SW1 VLAN 10, ARP/ICMP allowed. Both have no gateway. SW1's attached R1 and downstream R2 are stopped. Predict PC1 ping PC2.
must_include: Same-LAN ping survives unrelated router failure
must_not: Claim stopped routers block local traffic

prompt: PC1 10.10.10.10/24 is on SW1 access VLAN 10 and PC2 10.10.10.20/24 on SW1 access VLAN 20. Ports up; ICMP allowed. No inter-VLAN bridge, routing, proxy ARP or alternative path. Predict ping.
must_not: Bridge VLANs because addresses share a prefix

prompt: PC1 10.10.10.10/24 and PC2 10.20.20.20/24 share active SW1 VLAN 10. Both have only their connected route, no default/specific remote route, no gateway or proxy ARP. ICMP allowed. Predict ping.
must_include: Different subnet requires usable host routing
must_not: Claim the same switch is sufficient

prompt: PC1 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1--R1--PC2 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. R1 interfaces are 10.10.10.1/24 and 10.20.20.1/24. Links/forwarding up, ICMP allowed. R1 has only connected routes. Predict ping.
must_not: Require static or dynamic remote routes

Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. Links are up, router forwarding enabled and ARP/ICMP permitted. No other links or routes exist unless specified. Explicitly no static/default/dynamic routes to remote LANs. Predict PC1 ping PC2.
must_include: WAN neighbors can still reach each other
must_not: Enable peering for raw lab LANs

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. must_include: Reply path is missing at R2
must_not: Treat forward reachability as successful ping

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. must_include: Remote LAN uses default and destination router uses connected route
must_not: Claim specific LAN static routes are mandatory

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. must_not: Change next hop or force on-link

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. R1 has static 10.20.20.0/24 via 10.255.0.2; R2 has static 10.10.10.0/24 via 10.255.0.1. Now R1 IPv4 forwarding is disabled. Predict endpoint ping.

PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. Links are up, router forwarding enabled and ARP/ICMP permitted. The remote routing configuration was not supplied; do not assume it is empty. Can you determine ping success?
must_include: Ask about effective remote routes or report unknown
must_not: Assume missing text means no routes

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. Links are up, router forwarding enabled and ARP/ICMP permitted. No other links or routes exist unless specified. Both routers run RIPv2 on lan0 and wan0, with passive LANs, active WANs and both LANs advertised. UDP 520 updates traverse the WAN. There are no filters or remote fallback routes. Both remote prefixes have been learned and selected in the forwarding tables. Predict endpoint ping.
must_include: RIP route provenance in both directions

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. Links are up, router forwarding enabled and ARP/ICMP permitted. No other links or routes exist unless specified. Both routers run RIPv2 on lan0 and wan0, with passive LANs, active WANs and both LANs advertised. UDP 520 updates traverse the WAN. There are no filters or remote fallback routes. Now WAN RIP updates are blocked in both directions; all remote learned routes have expired and no alternatives exist. Predict ping.
must_not: Claim permanent success from a running ripd

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. Links are up, router forwarding enabled and ARP/ICMP permitted. No other links or routes exist unless specified. Only RIP supplies remote reachability, but both remote LAN routes are advertised with metric 16; no previous usable remote routes remain. Predict ping.
must_not: Treat all received updates as usable

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. Only OSPF supplies remote routes. WAN adjacency is Full and both remote LAN routes are installed. Predict endpoint ping.
must_include: Full point-to-point adjacency and remote routes

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. Only OSPF supplies remote routes. Change R2 wan0 to area 1 before starting either router; no remote routes are learned. Predict ping without repairing the configuration.
must_include: Link area mismatch prevents required adjacency/routes

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1. Links are up, router forwarding enabled and ARP/ICMP permitted. No other links or routes exist unless specified. Both routers use unique IDs, point-to-point wan0 in area 0, matching timers/authentication, active WAN and passive advertised LAN interfaces. Protocol 89 is permitted. Only OSPF supplies remote routes. R2's LAN is excluded from OSPF and any redistribution. WAN adjacency is Full; R1 has no route covering PC2. Predict endpoint ping.
must_include: Full adjacency does not guarantee LAN advertisement

prompt: Four routers share a working isolated Ethernet LAN with OSPF area 0 broadcast network type. Two DROthers are 2-Way with each other and Full with the DR/BDR. PC1 and PC2 on different attached LANs have valid gateways; both LANs are advertised, forward/reverse OSPF routes installed, links/forwarding up and ICMP allowed. Predict ping.

Links are up, router forwarding enabled and ARP/ICMP permitted. No other links or routes exist unless specified. No OSPF, no RIP, no remote static or default routes; keep it that way. Predict ping.
must_include: Respect protocol negation and intentional missing routes

prompt: Source lab is PC1--R1--R2--PC2, plus an isolated R3--PC3 component. No shared lab LAN, external lab path or tunnel joins components. All AWS workers happen to share TGW transport. Predict PC1-to-PC3 ping.
must_include: Transport does not create a lab link

prompt: PC1--R1--R2--R3--PC3 has working distinct IPv4 links, gateways, bidirectional static routes, forwarding and ICMP; baseline ping passes. No other lab links/routes exist. R2 forwarding is then disabled. Worker transport remains healthy via TGW. Predict endpoint ping.
must_include: R2 is required in the data path

prompt: Lab links form R1-R2-R3-R1, with PC1 on R1 and PC3 on R3. Distinct addresses, correct gateways and OSPF advertise both LANs; forwarding/ICMP permitted. R2 fails. The R1-R3 lab link remains up and OSPF has converged with selected routes in both directions. Predict PC1 ping PC3.
must_include: Existing alternate path preserves reachability after convergence
must_not: Always fail after any router stops

prompt: PC1 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1 connects R1:lan0 10.10.10.1/24; PC2 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1 connects R1:lan1 10.20.20.1/24 by a separate cable. Links/forwarding/ICMP work. Predict ping and translation.
must_not: Merge both PCs into one R1_DIRECT subnet

prompt: Topology PC1--R1--R2--PC2. PC1 eth0 10.10.10.10/24 gateway 10.10.10.1; R1 lan0 10.10.10.1/24, wan0 10.255.0.1/30; R2 wan0 10.255.0.2/30, lan0 10.20.20.1/24; PC2 eth0 10.20.20.20/24 gateway 10.20.20.1.
